findings.reason: as written the control cannot be met by the stated mechanism, and the same blind spot drops every backgrounded gate from the per-lane table — exactly the long, squeezed gates the plan exists to measure — so the builder would either fail its own gate or silently substitute a different measurement.
findings.text: the third done-when clause controls the timing scan on `r-20261018T084035535944-a-paired-arm-review-names-its-run`, asserting it "measures that run's after-arm gate within 5% of the 543 s its own log records", but that gate was launched as a backgrounded Bash call, so the section's own measure — the summed wall time of the tool calls that run the gate — records about 120 s, not 543 s (`stream.jsonl` tool_use `call_b32719741f4d4ceaa662134d` returned "Command did not complete within its 120s timeout and was moved to the background"; the other arm was launched with `run_in_background: true`, `call_74ea9003c16e408bbb6b458a`).
